summary: This document defines and registers with IANA a URN namespace for use within messages standardized by the Eurosystem. Deutsche Bundesbank, a member of the European System of Central Banks, manages the namespace.

plainLanguage.summary: This sets aside a special name prefix for messages used by European central banks.

questions: how to register a urn namespace
subtitle: A registered namespace for identifying Eurosystem financial messaging resources

tldr.problem: Eurosystem's financial messaging platforms need persistent, stable identifiers for resources like message schemas and data definitions that will remain valid for decades after a message is exchanged.
tldr.mechanism: The document registers a Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace with IANA, allowing the Eurosystem to assign and manage identifiers following RFC 3406 procedures, starting with TARGET2-Securities messages.
tldr.outcome: The 'eurosystem' URN namespace is now an official IANA registry, enabling the Eurosystem to persistently identify messaging resources under its own control.

today: RFC 7207 is an Informational RFC that established the 'eurosystem' URN namespace with IANA in 2014. This namespace remains active and is used by the Eurosystem to identify TARGET2-Securities messaging resources and potentially other future Eurosystem projects.

sections.title: The Eurosystem and TARGET2-Securities
sections.content:
The European System of Central Banks (ESCB) consists of the European Central Bank (ECB) and the central banks of all 27 EU member states. The Eurosystem specifically refers to the ECB and those central banks whose countries have adopted the Euro currency.

The Eurosystem operates several critical financial infrastructure systems. TARGET2 is the real-time gross settlement system for cross-border transfers throughout the EU. TARGET2-Securities (T2S) is a harmonized, centralized platform for settling securities in central bank money, being developed by Deutsche Bundesbank, Banque de France, Banca d'Italia, and Banco de Espana. These systems exchange messages following the ISO 20022 standard, an international specification for financial industry messages. This document creates a URN namespace for identifying the resources (schemas, entity types, message definitions) used in these messaging systems.
sections.plainLanguage: European central banks run big systems for moving money and securities. The messages in these systems follow international rules, but they also need their own special naming system so that ten years from now, people can still find the exact schema that was used for a particular message.

sections.title: Uniform Resource Names and Namespaces
sections.content:
Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) are the abstract concept of identifying resources on the internet. A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is one type of URI that specifies where a resource lives (like http://example.com). A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is another type of URI that assigns a persistent identifier to a resource independent of its location. URNs follow the format urn:nid:nss, where nid is the namespace identifier and nss is the namespace-specific string.

For example, RFC 3986 defines how URIs work syntactically. RFC 3406 defines the process for registering formal URN namespaces with IANA. This allows organizations to request their own namespace (like 'eurosystem') and define how identifiers within that namespace are structured and managed. Once registered, an organization has perpetual control of its namespace and can assign identifiers without risk of collision with other organizations.
sections.plainLanguage: A URN is like a permanent ID number. It says "this is the ISO schema version 2.1 for bank transfer messages" and that ID never changes, even if the physical file moves to a different computer.

sections.title: Scope and Community Considerations
sections.content:
The Eurosystem requested the URN namespace identifier 'eurosystem' to identify resources related to Eurosystem messaging. The namespace is reserved to the Eurosystem and its community. Initially, the namespace will be populated with identifiers for resources used in TARGET2-Securities messaging, such as XML schemas, message type definitions, and data element definitions.

A key consideration is community transparency. Even though Eurosystem messages are often transmitted in encrypted digital envelopes or Virtual Private Networks, the resources being identified are referred to and resolved on the public internet. This transparency is important for maintaining public trust in financial systems, enabling open software development, and supporting software deployment. For this reason, the Eurosystem URN namespace is resolvable publicly, and the authority behind the namespace is clearly identified. This puts Eurosystem URNs at the same perceived authority level as other international treaty organization URN namespaces.
sections.plainLanguage: The Eurosystem namespace is public so that anyone can look up what a particular URN refers to, even though the actual messages might be secret. This keeps the financial system transparent and trustworthy.

sections.title: Formal Namespace Registration
sections.content:
The registration template in the RFC specifies the details of the 'eurosystem' namespace. The Namespace ID is 'eurosystem'. The scope includes resources related to Eurosystem messaging. The registrant is Deutsche Bundesbank, acting on behalf of the Eurosystem. The contact person is Miriam Ortseifen at Deutsche Bundesbank's T2S Service Management group.

The Namespace Specific String (NSS) within the eurosystem namespace follows a flat space of printable URI characters, with a preference for short, letter-digit-period-hyphen-based strings. For example, 'urn:eurosystem:xsd:reda.012.001.01' identifies an XML schema definition. The namespace has no knowable structure outside the context of the Eurosystem's internal resolver. Identifiers are uniquely assigned by Eurosystem URN Registration, and assigned URNs will not be reused; they remain valid even if the referenced resource's status changes.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration says: the Eurosystem owns all IDs starting with 'urn:eurosystem:'; Deutsche Bundesbank controls them; and the IDs follow simple rules like 'xsd:' for schemas or 'msg:' for message types.

sections.title: Resolution and Operational Procedures
sections.content:
Eurosystem URNs are resolved through URN resolvers run under Eurosystem responsibility. Initially, resolution service is provided through a web page listing assigned names and the related metadata of the named resources. The Eurosystem maintains control of the assignment process; names are granted through Eurosystem URN Registration via proprietary procedures.

Since the URNs are opaque (their structure reveals nothing about the resource), there are no additional security considerations beyond those normally associated with URI and URN use. However, attempting to resolve a Eurosystem URN through a resolver other than the one provided by the Eurosystem is error-prone and not considered authoritative. For practical purposes, only the official Eurosystem resolver should be trusted for Eurosystem URN resolution.
sections.plainLanguage: The Eurosystem keeps a list of all its URNs and what they point to. If you want to know what 'urn:eurosystem:xsd:reda.012.001.01' means, you ask the Eurosystem's official resolver, not some other resolver online.
